title: MMT of the Hip, Knee and Ankle — Gluteals, Quadriceps and the Calf

hook.en: The legs are the strongest muscles in the body, so the standard hands-on test often says "5/5" when real strength is missing. Learn the correct positions, the Trendelenburg link and why the calf is tested by heel raises.
hook.ur: Taangein jism ke sab se mazboot muscles hain, is liye standard hands-on test aksar “5/5” kehta hai jab asal taqat kam hoti hai. Sahi positions, Trendelenburg ka link aur calf heel raises se kyun test hota hai seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll test gluteus medius, gluteus maximus, quadriceps and the calf with correct positions and resistance, name the substitution for each and use functional tests for the big muscles.
goal.ur: End tak aap gluteus medius, gluteus maximus, quadriceps aur calf ko sahi position aur resistance se test karenge, har ek ki substitution batayenge aur bare muscles ke liye functional tests use karenge.

text.en: Four lower-limb muscle groups matter most. **Gluteus medius** (superior gluteal nerve, L4–S1) keeps the pelvis level when you stand on one leg. **Gluteus maximus** (inferior gluteal nerve, L5–S2) extends the hip for stairs and sit-to-stand. **Quadriceps** (femoral nerve, L2–L4) straightens the knee. **Calf** (gastrocnemius and soleus, tibial nerve S1–S2) pushes you off the ground when you walk. Each has a standard position and a classic cheat.
text.ur: Lower limb ke chaar muscle groups sab se ahem hain. **Gluteus medius** (superior gluteal nerve, L4–S1) ek taang par khare hone par pelvis ko level rakhta hai. **Gluteus maximus** (inferior gluteal nerve, L5–S2) seerhiyon aur sit-to-stand ke liye hip ko extend karta hai. **Quadriceps** (femoral nerve, L2–L4) knee ko seedha karta hai. **Calf** (gastrocnemius aur soleus, tibial nerve S1–S2) chalte waqt aap ko zameen se push-off deta hai. Har ek ki standard position aur classic cheat hai.

text.en: Think of gluteus medius as the guy-ropes of a tent pole. When you stand on one leg, the ropes on the stance side stop the pole (the pelvis) from falling to the other side. If the ropes are weak, the pole drops — that is the Trendelenburg sign.
text.ur: Gluteus medius ko khaime ke khambay ki rassiyan samjhein. Ek taang par khare hone par stance side ki rassiyan khambay (pelvis) ko doosri taraf girne se rokti hain. Rassiyan kamzor hon to khamba gir jata hai — yehi Trendelenburg sign hai.

intro.en: Side-lying on the untested side with the lower leg bent, the patient lifts the top leg **slightly behind the midline** (a little extension isolates the gluteus medius). The examiner resists on the lateral distal thigh. Watch for the leg drifting forward (TFL), hiking the hip (quadratus lumborum) and rolling back.
intro.ur: Untested side par side-lying, neeche wali taang mori hui, patient oopar wali taang ko **midline se thora peechay** uthata hai (thora extension gluteus medius ko isolate karta hai). Examiner lateral distal thigh par resist karta hai. Taang ke aage bhatakne (TFL), hip hiking (quadratus lumborum) aur peechay lurakne par nazar rakhein.

question.en: In the hip abduction test, the patient's leg drifts forward and rotates as it rises. Which muscle is substituting?
question.ur: Hip abduction test mein patient ki taang uthte hue aage bhatakti aur ghoomti hai. Kaun sa muscle substitute kar raha hai?

text.en: Tensor fasciae latae (and hip flexors) for a weak gluteus medius
text.ur: Kamzor gluteus medius ki jagah tensor fasciae latae (aur hip flexors)

feedback.en: Yes — TFL abducts with flexion and internal rotation, so a leg that drifts forward is the cheat. Keep the hip slightly extended and neutral.
feedback.ur: Haan — TFL flexion aur internal rotation ke saath abduct karta hai, is liye aage bhatakti taang cheat hai. Hip ko thora extended aur neutral rakhein.

feedback.en: Maximus extends and externally rotates; it would not cause forward drift.
feedback.ur: Maximus extend aur externally rotate karta hai; aage drift nahi karta.
Adductors abduction ke khilaf kaam karte hain.

intro.en: Prone with the knee bent 90° to isolate the gluteus maximus (knee straight adds the hamstrings). The patient lifts the thigh toward the ceiling while the examiner resists on the back of the distal thigh. The common cheat is the lower back arching and the pelvis rotating.
intro.ur: Prone, knee 90° mora hua taake gluteus maximus isolate ho (knee seedha ho to hamstrings bhi shamil). Patient thigh ko chhat ki taraf uthata hai aur examiner distal thigh ki peeth par resist karta hai. Aam cheat kamar ka arch hona aur pelvis ka ghoomna hai.

intro.en: Sitting with a towel under the distal thigh, the patient straightens the knee **without locking it**; the examiner resists at the front of the leg above the ankle. Locking the knee gives a false strong result, and leaning back lets the hip flexors help.
intro.ur: Distal thigh ke neeche towel ke saath baithe hue patient knee ko **lock kiye bagair** seedha karta hai; examiner ankle ke upar samne resist karta hai. Knee lock karne se jhoota mazboot result aata hai, aur peechay jhukne se hip flexors madad kar dete hain.

rows.en: Side-lying, test hip slightly extended; resist on the lateral distal thigh
rows.ur: Side-lying, test hip thora extended; lateral distal thigh par resist

rows.en: TFL (leg drifts forward), quadratus lumborum (hip hike), rolling back
rows.ur: TFL (taang aage bhatakti), quadratus lumborum (hip hike), peechay lurakna

rows.en: Prone, knee bent 90°; resist on the back of the distal thigh
rows.ur: Prone, knee 90° mora hua; distal thigh ki peeth par resist

rows.en: Lumbar extension and pelvic rotation (the back arches)
rows.ur: Lumbar extension aur pelvic rotation (kamar arch)

rows.en: Sitting, towel under the thigh; resist on the front of the leg above the ankle
rows.ur: Baithe hue, thigh ke neeche towel; ankle ke upar samne resist

rows.en: Leaning back, hip internal rotation, locking the knee
rows.ur: Peechay jhukna, hip internal rotation, knee lock karna

rows.en: Standing, single-leg heel raise through full range, repeated
rows.ur: Khare hokar, single-leg heel raise poori range mein, baar baar

rows.en: Toe flexors, tibialis posterior, peroneals and leaning forward
rows.ur: Toe flexors, tibialis posterior, peroneals aur aage jhukna

text.en: **Testing the calf with your hands.** The gastrocnemius and soleus are so strong that no examiner can resist them by hand: pushing on the sole will always "break" a normal calf. The right test is the **single-leg heel raise**, standing with fingertips on a wall for balance. Count the full-range raises: about 20–25 is normal (editions differ), fewer than that is weakness, and one full raise is grade 3. Do not count raises that stop short of full range.
text.ur: **Calf ko haathon se test karna.** Gastrocnemius aur soleus itne mazboot hain ke koi examiner haath se unhein resist nahi kar sakta: sole par dabane se normal calf bhi hamesha “toot” jata hai. Sahi test **single-leg heel raise** hai, khare hokar, balance ke liye fingertips deewar par. Poori range wali raises ginein: takriban 20–25 normal hain (editions mein farq), isse kam kamzori, aur ek poori raise grade 3. Adhoori range par ruk jane wali raises na ginein.

question.en: How do you grade calf strength reliably?
question.ur: Calf ki taqat reliably kaise grade karte hain?

text.en: Count full single-leg heel raises (about 20–25 is normal; one raise is grade 3)
text.ur: Poori single-leg heel raises ginein (takriban 20–25 normal; ek raise grade 3)

feedback.en: Yes — functional testing for large muscles is more valid than hand resistance.
feedback.ur: Haan — bare muscles ke liye functional testing haath ki resistance se zyada valid hai.

text.en: Push on the sole with your hand

feedback.en: Your hand cannot overcome a normal calf, so every patient looks weak.
feedback.ur: Aap ka haath normal calf ko nahi hara sakta, is liye har patient kamzor lagega.

text.en: Ask the patient to push their foot into the floor
text.ur: Patient se foot ko zameen mein dabane ko kahein

feedback.en: That is not quantifiable and ignores range.
feedback.ur: Yeh naapa nahi ja sakta aur range ko nazar-andaz karta hai.

text.en: **Trendelenburg and the gluteal gap.** In single-leg stance a weak gluteus medius lets the opposite pelvis drop (Trendelenburg) or the trunk lean over the stance hip to compensate (a compensated Trendelenburg). Gluteal weakness is common after hip surgery, in hip osteoarthritis, lateral hip pain (gluteal tendinopathy) and after deep gluteal injections. Treat with progressive loading from side-lying abduction to step-downs, and test again in single-leg stance for 30 seconds.
text.ur: **Trendelenburg aur gluteal gap.** Single-leg stance mein kamzor gluteus medius opposite pelvis ko girne deta hai (Trendelenburg) ya trunk ko stance hip ke upar jhuka kar compensate karta hai (compensated Trendelenburg). Gluteal kamzori hip surgery ke baad, hip osteoarthritis, lateral hip pain (gluteal tendinopathy) aur deep gluteal injections ke baad aam hai. Side-lying abduction se step-downs tak progressive loading se ilaaj karein, aur 30 seconds ki single-leg stance mein dobara test karein.

text.en: In the knee extensors, manual grade 5 can hide a strength deficit of **20–50%** compared with a dynamometer, so for return-to-sport decisions (for example after ACL reconstruction) a limb symmetry index above 90% on a hand-held dynamometer or isokinetic test is preferred to "5/5". The 30-second chair stand and single-leg heel-raise test are cheap and valid functional alternatives for older adults and calf strength.
text.ur: Knee extensors mein manual grade 5 dynamometer ke muqable mein **20–50 %** taqat ki kami chhupa sakta hai, is liye return-to-sport faislon (maslan ACL reconstruction ke baad) mein “5/5” ke bajaye hand-held dynamometer ya isokinetic test par limb symmetry index 90 % se upar behtar hai. 30-second chair stand aur single-leg heel-raise test sasti aur valid functional alternatives hain buzurgon aur calf strength ke liye.

question.en: A patient stands on the right leg and their left pelvis drops. Which side is the weak gluteus medius?
question.ur: Patient right taang par khara hota hai aur uska left pelvis gir jata hai. Kamzor gluteus medius kaun si side ka hai?

answer.en: The **right** (stance-side) gluteus medius. The weak muscle is on the side the patient is standing on; the pelvis drops on the opposite side.
answer.ur: **Right** (stance-side) gluteus medius. Kamzor muscle us side ka hai jis par patient khara hai; pelvis opposite side gir jata hai.

question.en: Which position isolates the gluteus maximus rather than the hamstrings?
question.ur: Kaun si position hamstrings ke bajaye gluteus maximus ko isolate karti hai?

feedback.en: Yes — a bent knee slackens the hamstrings so the glute does the work.
feedback.ur: Haan — mora hua knee hamstrings ko dheela karta hai to glute kaam karta hai.

feedback.en: A straight knee includes the hamstrings.
feedback.ur: Seedha knee hamstrings ko shamil karta hai.

text.en: **Stop and refer** if a leg is suddenly weak after a fall or hip pain (possible fracture), if resisted testing reproduces sharp groin pain (hip pathology), if weakness comes with back pain and bladder or bowel symptoms (cauda equina), or if the calf is swollen, red and tender (DVT). Avoid resisted testing within the early post-operative protocol period unless your surgeon allows it.
text.ur: **Ruk jayein aur refer karein** agar girne ya hip ke dard ke baad taang achanak kamzor ho (shayad fracture), resisted testing se groin mein tez dard dubara ho (hip ki bimari), kamzori kamar ke dard aur bladder ya bowel symptoms ke saath ho (cauda equina), ya calf sooji, laal aur tender ho (DVT). Surgeon ki ijazat ke bagair early post-operative protocol mein resisted testing se bachein.

summary.en: Gluteus medius (side-lying, slightly extended), gluteus maximus (prone, knee bent), quadriceps (sitting, no knee lock) have standard positions and classic cheats (TFL, back arch, leaning back).
summary.ur: Gluteus medius (side-lying, thora extended), gluteus maximus (prone, knee mora hua), quadriceps (baithe hue, knee lock nahi) ki standard positions aur classic cheats (TFL, kamar arch, peechay jhukna) hain.

summary.en: Test the calf with single-leg heel raises, not hands; use dynamometry or 30-second chair stand when "5/5" is not enough.
summary.ur: Calf ko single-leg heel raises se test karein, haathon se nahi; jab “5/5” kaafi na ho to dynamometry ya 30-second chair stand use karein.

summary.en: Trendelenburg drops the pelvis on the side opposite the weak stance-side gluteus medius; refer sudden weakness, groin pain, cauda equina signs and a swollen calf.
summary.ur: Trendelenburg weak stance-side gluteus medius ki opposite side pelvis girata hai; achanak kamzori, groin dard, cauda equina signs aur sooji calf refer karein.

front.en: Nerve supply of gluteus medius, gluteus maximus, quadriceps and calf?
front.ur: Gluteus medius, gluteus maximus, quadriceps aur calf ki nerve supply?

back.en: Superior gluteal (L4–S1), inferior gluteal (L5–S2), femoral (L2–L4) and tibial (S1–S2).
back.ur: Superior gluteal (L4–S1), inferior gluteal (L5–S2), femoral (L2–L4) aur tibial (S1–S2).

back.en: Single-leg heel raises through full range, counted (about 20–25 is normal; one raise is grade 3).
back.ur: Single-leg heel raises poori range mein, ginti ke saath (takriban 20–25 normal; ek raise grade 3).

front.en: What substitution in hip abduction makes the leg drift forward?
front.ur: Hip abduction mein kaun si substitution taang ko aage bhatkati hai?
Trendelenburg mein kaun si side girti hai?

back.en: The pelvis on the opposite side of the weak stance-side gluteus medius.
back.ur: Weak stance-side gluteus medius ki opposite side ka pelvis.
